b243.content: A plain and friendly explanation of Catholic belief written for American Protestants by the archbishop of Baltimore. It covers the Church, the papacy, the saints, the sacraments, and purgatory, and became one of the best-selling Catholic books in American history.

b245.content: A historical novel of the Elizabethan persecution in Derbyshire, where young Robin Audrey and Marjorie Manners give up their hopes of marriage so that Robin can become a priest in a land where saying Mass is punished by death.

b247.content: A companion to Lord of the World. Where that novel imagined the world turning away from Christ, this one imagines a future in which the Church has regained the allegiance of the nations, and asks what such a world would demand of its people.

b258.content: A vivid account of the Passion of Christ drawn from the visions of Bl. Anne Catherine Emmerich, as written down by the poet Clemens Brentano. It has fed the devotion of many readers, though scholars note that Brentano shaped and added to what he recorded, and the Church did not consider the visions in her beatification.

b268.content: Seven short devotional treatises first printed by Henry Pepwell in 1521, including passages from St. Catherine of Siena, Walter Hilton, the author of The Cloud of Unknowing, and Margery Kempe. Edited by Edmund Gardner (1910).

b270.content:
The German Jesuit Joseph Deharbe wrote one of the most widely used catechisms of the nineteenth century, taught for generations in Germany and among German-speaking Catholics in America.

This fuller edition opens with a short history of revealed religion, from Adam to the modern Church, then explains the Creed, the Commandments, and the means of grace, the sacraments and prayer, in numbered questions and answers with Scripture for each.

b271.content:
The shortest of the Baltimore Catechisms, prepared for children getting ready for their First Communion. In 33 short lessons of questions and answers it covers God and creation, sin and redemption, the Church, the sacraments, prayer, and the commandments.

Its questions are numbered to match the fuller No. 2, and it closes with morning and evening prayers, prayers for Mass and Communion, the Rosary, and hymns.

b272.content:
The advanced Baltimore Catechism, written as a two-year course for students after Confirmation. It includes the questions of No. 2 and adds many more that explain them, defining terms and giving the reasons behind each teaching.

It follows the same 37 lessons, from the end of man to the last things.

b273.content:
Written for Sunday-school teachers and older students, and often called Baltimore Catechism No. 4. It goes through the catechism question by question, explaining each answer in plain words with examples from everyday life.

Its homely comparisons, like a watch made to keep time and a pen made to write, made it a favorite of teachers for decades.
